method: Coordinator read actual public dictionary entries through web_fetch. Bounded paraphrases below identify exact headings/senses and returned extraction limits; complete copyrighted web pages are not reproduced. Frozen complete JMdict families and raw KANJIDIC2 records are separate licensed evidence.

sources: 精選版 日本国語大辞典
verifiedClaims: Seisenban plant sense describes generally smaller bamboos, stem sheaths retained compared with take, use of leaves to wrap foods and ornamental garden planting. Its numerical size description is not imported as a universal size threshold.
Sense 2 records the alcohol sense as 女房詞, old court-language vocabulary, with historical citations; it is not recast as an ordinary modern drink request.
Other senses concern crests and theatrical/ritual implements. These are recognized but not expanded into this plant lesson.
Jitsu identifies the character as 国字 and explicitly says its origin is unclear. Its speculative leaf-shape or sound derivations are not taught as fact.
The early plant citation uses a phonetic ささ gloss; it supports a historical native plant word, not a universal derivation or popularity ranking.
entries.limits: Digital Daijisen and animal/plant dictionary headings were returned without their definitions. Verification uses only the actually returned Seisenban/Jitsu sections, not empty headings.

sources: 精選版 日本国語大辞典
verifiedClaims: Daijisen and Seisenban distinguish the muku tree/fruit sense from an abbreviation of mukudori. The tree-only frozen JMdict family does not override these documented secondary senses.
Jitsu gives 字音 リョウ（リャウ） and むくのき as the character gloss, independently of guessing a kana substring in a compound.
Jitsu identifies 京 as phonetic in its analysis. Teaching conservatively uses a labelled modern-shape mnemonic and structure-unclassified instead of adding historical analysis.
entries.limits: Some historical glyphs in Jitsu were images, not decoded text. They are not reproduced, assigned readings or used as word examples.

sources: 動植物名よみかた辞典 普及版
verifiedClaims: Jitsu explicitly lists 椋樹 with its りようじゆ reading and the muku-tree gloss. Teaching normalizes full-size kana to modern small-kana りょうじゅ, consistently with the separate character 字音 リョウ.
The independent plant-name section gives ムクノキ and Aphananthe aspera. Different source readings of the same spelling remain separate; the kun plant name does not invalidate the on compound.
The attested on compound is recognition-only in this bounded plant lesson; it is not declared nonexistent, common or a selected question.
entries.limits: Dictionary recognition, not frequency or a measured everyday-use claim. The older plant classification is not imported into teaching.

headings: むく‐の‐き【×椋の木／×樸の▽樹】
sources: 精選版 日本国語大辞典
verifiedClaims: Both entries describe a deciduous tall tree and rough leaves used for polishing, and give むく as an alternative name.
The fruit is described as ripening black. No food-safety advice, unrestricted edibility recommendation or new fruit article is authored.
Seisenban's early phonetic plant citation and alternative むく support the native plant-name layer without deriving it from the kanji.
The sources use different botanical family classifications. This narrow lesson identifies Aphananthe aspera and avoids a family-classification claim.
entries.limits: Source descriptions support the rough-leaf/deciduous examples; natural original learner sentences are not misrepresented as verbatim upstream attestations.

sources: 精選版 日本国語大辞典
verifiedClaims: Both entries identify a boat made by folding a sasa leaf; Seisenban explains floating it in a river for play.
The separate light/small-boat extension is recognized but not used to turn every small boat into a leaf boat.
entries.limits: The first coordinator request used an incorrect numeric suffix 510069 and redirected to 左近衛中将, not 笹舟. That successful but irrelevant fetch was rejected as evidence. A fresh bare-headword lookup resolved to this actual 510203 entry; no plausible URL was counted as verification.

sources: 精選版 日本国語大辞典
verifiedClaims: The actual bird sense and explanation that the name relates to liking muku fruit were returned. This is lexical-name evidence, not character etymology.
Separate historical mocking-person, migrant-worker and inexperienced-trader senses are not neutral bird synonyms and are not expanded here.
entries.limits: Digital Daijisen/Jitsu/animal-name headings lacked body text in this extraction. No missing body is claimed read; the source citation uses Seisenban only.

limits: External dictionary inspection and bounded author decisions are not independent content review, native-speaker certification, live-quiz safety, frequency evidence or phone acceptance.
